Former Synagogue in Heinsheim (Bad Rappenau)

Former Synagogue · Bad Rappenau, Germany

The synagogue in Heinsheim, now part of Bad Rappenau, was built around 1795-96 in an understated style reflecting restrictions placed on Jewish congregations at the time. The small Jewish community dissolved in November 1937, and the building was sold to a farmer before the November 1938 pogrom, which is why it was not destroyed. It was later used as a locksmith's workshop. In 2012 a local association, Freundeskreis Ehemalige Synagoge Heinsheim e.V., was formed to preserve the building, acquiring it in 2013. Restoration work is underway to convert the former synagogue into a memorial and cultural meeting space.
